_authoring.source: Season 1 Script Bible scene map for Episode 2. Beats, cast and choice architecture are the Creative Director's; dialogue expanded for the web build.
_authoring.spine: The pool scene is the emotional spine of the season. Everything before it exists to earn it; everything after exists because of it. No music. The silences are real `is_hold` beats, not described.
_authoring.titleRule: The episode title is played completely straight in the Nexus scene. No irony. This is what Fiz stands to lose.
_authoring.continuity: Lines carry `requires` / `unless` on Episode 1 consequence ids so the hallway choice changes what people say here.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Forty thousand by first period. I know the number because six different people made sure I knew the number.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mason Cranstain
dialogue_sequence.text: Forty thousand. Forty. This school has four hundred people in it. Where are the other thirty-nine thousand six hundred coming from?

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Pete Lindson
dialogue_sequence.text: Everywhere. That's the answer. It stopped being about Blackwell around eight this morning.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (It's Riley alone in the frame. Just her. Nobody standing anywhere near her, which is accurate, and which is the part I keep having to look at.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I'm in the edge of the frame for four of the nine seconds. Cropped so it looks like I'm walking past.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: It's cut so it looks like I'm crying. I wasn't crying. I was telling her to get the phone out of my face.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: He took that out. The audio's a song now.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Maddie Hale
dialogue_sequence.text: It's on my side of the internet too. People I've streamed with are quote-posting it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Maddie Hale
dialogue_sequence.text: Somebody in my chat last night said 'do the Riley face.' In my chat. Like it's a thing that exists now.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Amber Clarke
dialogue_sequence.text: MORNING, table! Big morning for us! Huge numbers!

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: Amber, don't. Genuinely, don't, you're making it worse.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He edited it. He's telling her off for enjoying it. Both of those are true at the same time and neither of them costs him anything.)

choices.choice_text: [Ask Maddie to post something. Her audience, her voice.]
[Say nothing here. Go after the source file.]
[Wait until Chase is on his own.]

ep2_report_official.speaker: Pete Lindson
ep2_report_official.text: Carter will thank you for bringing it to him and then it'll be a Blackwell matter, and Blackwell matters go in a drawer.

ep2_report_official.speaker: Fiz
ep2_report_official.text: (Carter listened for eleven minutes. He wrote nothing down. He said the phrase 'proportionate response' twice.)

ep2_report_official.speaker: Fiz
ep2_report_official.text: (Marcus was on the door when I came out. He'd heard all of it. He logged it anyway, in his own book, in his own handwriting. He didn't tell me he was doing that — I saw the page.)

ep2_maddie_defends.speaker: Maddie Hale
ep2_maddie_defends.text: Yeah. Yeah, okay. It's my platform, that's — yeah, that's the argument, isn't it.

ep2_maddie_defends.speaker: Maddie Hale
ep2_maddie_defends.text: I'll lose people. Not a lot. Some.

ep2_maddie_defends.speaker: Maddie Hale
ep2_maddie_defends.text: Doing it anyway. Don't say anything nice to me about it, I'll cry and I'm on in ten minutes.

ep2_maddie_defends.speaker: Fiz
ep2_maddie_defends.text: (She was down four hundred and eleven Locks by Sunday. She never mentioned it. I only know because I have the tab open while I edit.)

ep2_fiz_goes_technical.speaker: Fiz
ep2_fiz_goes_technical.text: (Nothing at this table is going to fix it. Everything at this table is going to make Amber's week.)

ep2_fiz_goes_technical.speaker: Fiz
ep2_fiz_goes_technical.text: (The clip has a re-encode signature. Everything does. Whoever exported it did it twice, and the second pass came off a machine with an archive profile on it.)

ep2_fiz_goes_technical.speaker: Fiz
ep2_fiz_goes_technical.text: (That's a school machine. That's a thing I can follow.)

ep2_chase_civil_alone.speaker: Fiz
ep2_chase_civil_alone.text: (Fourth period. He's outside the media block on his own, and without an audience he stands completely differently.)

ep2_chase_civil_alone.speaker: Chase Whitmore
ep2_chase_civil_alone.text: If you're here to hit me, do it on the left, the right side's my good angle.

ep2_chase_civil_alone.speaker: Chase Whitmore
ep2_chase_civil_alone.text: I cut it in about nine minutes. That's the bit nobody gets. Nine minutes and it's her whole year now.

ep2_chase_civil_alone.speaker: Chase Whitmore
ep2_chase_civil_alone.text: Anyway. Can't take it down, it's not mine any more, that's how it works. You wouldn't get it.

ep2_chase_civil_alone.speaker: Fiz
ep2_chase_civil_alone.text: (He got it. That's the thing I'll keep. He understood it completely and then went to lunch.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Can we not do the meeting about me while I'm sitting at it? Please?

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mason Cranstain
dialogue_sequence.text: ...Yeah. Sorry, Riley.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She eats about four bites. Nobody comments on the four bites, because commenting on the four bites is another meeting about her.)

scenes.location: Nexus — the quiet room, voice channel

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Four people in a voice channel doing nothing. This is the best hour of my week and I have never said that out loud to any of them.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mason Cranstain
dialogue_sequence.text: Okay, okay — this one's important. This one changed my life at fourteen.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Pete Lindson
dialogue_sequence.text: Mason, that's the third song you've said that about tonight.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mason Cranstain
dialogue_sequence.text: I had a big year.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Maddie Hale
dialogue_sequence.text: It's peaking. Your levels. It's all red. It's been red for an hour, I just didn't want to be rude.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mason Cranstain
dialogue_sequence.text: That's the mix. That's how it's meant to sound.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Pete Lindson
dialogue_sequence.text: It is not how it's meant to sound.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Maddie Hale
dialogue_sequence.text: ...I like this. This bit. Where nobody's doing anything.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Pete Lindson
dialogue_sequence.text: Yeah.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Mason's music. Pete correcting him. Maddie falling asleep with her mic on. Nobody needs anything from me.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (There's a folder on this laptop with eleven frames in it, and it has been sitting there all night about four centimetres from this conversation.)

choices.choice_text: "There's something I need you three to look at."
[Not tonight. Let them have the night.]

ep2_circle_knows.speaker: Mason Cranstain
ep2_circle_knows.text: ...Okay. That's your serious voice. You've got about two serious voices and that's the bad one.

ep2_circle_knows.speaker: Fiz
ep2_circle_knows.text: (Screen share. Ninety seconds. Nobody says anything for the length of a whole song ending.)

ep2_circle_knows.speaker: Maddie Hale
ep2_circle_knows.text: I'm not sleepy any more. That's — I'm fully not sleepy any more.

ep2_circle_knows.speaker: Mason Cranstain
ep2_circle_knows.text: Right. So we're doing this. Whatever this is. Obviously we're doing it.

ep2_circle_knows.speaker: Fiz
ep2_circle_knows.text: (That was the last easy night and I spent it. I'd like to say I didn't know. I knew.)

ep2_circle_innocent.speaker: Fiz
ep2_circle_innocent.text: (I close the folder instead. Mason queues something worse than the last one. Pete objects on principle.)

ep2_circle_innocent.speaker: Maddie Hale
ep2_circle_innocent.text: 'Night, boys. Leave the channel open. I like the noise.

ep2_circle_innocent.speaker: Fiz
ep2_circle_innocent.text: (We leave it open. Three of them breathing into microphones in three different rooms, and me listening to it, and none of them knowing anything.)

ep2_circle_innocent.speaker: Fiz
ep2_circle_innocent.text: (I gave them one more night. I'm going to keep coming back to whether that was a kindness or just an easier thing to do.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (1:40 AM. Channel's still live. Somebody's chair creaks somewhere in Arcadia Bay and it comes out of my headphones like it happened in this room.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: Sorry — sorry, hi. You're the exchange student. Blackwell. Photography.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: Cheryl Brandstone, Arcadia Bay Gazette. I'm not here about the storm. Everyone assumes I'm here about the storm.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She said it too fast. She rehearsed the part where she says she isn't here about the storm.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: I'm doing a school piece. Reconstruction money, where it went, what Blackwell got. Boring. Genuinely boring, I'm not selling it well.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: But you're at the lighthouse a lot. And the east pier. And the lot behind the science block, which nobody photographs, because there's nothing there.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She's been watching where I go. Not following. Noticing. Those are different and I'm not sure which one is worse.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Linda has stopped wiping the counter. She's four metres away with a cloth in her hand, not wiping anything.)

choices.choice_text: "I take pictures of buildings. That's the whole story."
"What have you got? Show me first."
"Whatever you're doing — stop. For your own sake."

ep2_cheryl_rebuffed.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
ep2_cheryl_rebuffed.text: Right. Okay. That's fair, that's — I did ambush you at breakfast, so.

ep2_cheryl_rebuffed.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
ep2_cheryl_rebuffed.text: Card's on the table. I'm going to leave it there and you're going to leave it there, and that's fine.

ep2_cheryl_rebuffed.speaker: Fiz
ep2_cheryl_rebuffed.text: (She left it face up. She wanted me to have to turn it over to stop reading it.)

ep2_cheryl_alliance_early.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
ep2_cheryl_alliance_early.text: ...Really? Nobody says that. Everybody says 'no comment' like they've seen it in something.

ep2_cheryl_alliance_early.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
ep2_cheryl_alliance_early.text: Okay. Permits. Cross Industries doesn't own anything in this bay. Eleven companies own things, and Cross Industries owns a piece of every one of them, and none of the pieces are big enough to have to declare.

ep2_cheryl_alliance_early.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
ep2_cheryl_alliance_early.text: That's not illegal. That's just eleven decisions in a row that all point the same way.

ep2_cheryl_alliance_early.speaker: Fiz
ep2_cheryl_alliance_early.text: (She talks like someone who has had nobody to say this to. Which is exactly how she got to be alone with it.)

ep2_cheryl_warned.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
ep2_cheryl_warned.text: No — because my editor said something like that in October. In a nicer voice. With his hand on the door.

ep2_cheryl_warned.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
ep2_cheryl_warned.text: And I've noticed the people who tell me to stop are never the people who don't know anything.

ep2_cheryl_warned.speaker: Fiz
ep2_cheryl_warned.text: (I made it worse. I meant it kindly and I handed her a reason.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: Right. Thanks for the — yeah. Thanks.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (The bell over the door. Then nothing for a while.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
dialogue_sequence.text: More coffee, sweetheart?

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She hadn't refilled anybody the whole time that woman was sitting there. Not her. Not me. Not the two men by the window.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
dialogue_sequence.text: That girl's going to write something one day and this town's going to be very unkind to her about it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Linda Jacquelin
dialogue_sequence.text: Eat your eggs.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (The side door's been broken since October. Everybody knows. Nobody's fixed it, which in this town is practically a policy.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: This is stupid. This is so stupid. I want that on the record before anything happens.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: 'Girl, seventeen, drowns in four feet of water at eleven at night for no reason.'

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She's got her arms crossed over the swimsuit and she hasn't come past the third tile.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I don't tell her it's fine. People have been telling her it's fine her whole life and it hasn't worked once.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I get in. Shallow end. And then I don't do anything at all.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: You're not going to say anything?

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Everybody says something. There's a whole speech. 'Just relax, it's easy, I've got you.'

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: ...Okay, well, now you're just being weird at me.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Fourth tile. Then the step. Then she stands on the first step for a long time with the water at her ankles like it's an argument she's having.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: I was six. That's all. Everyone was running and someone picked me up and then I was in it, and I don't remember being taken out.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: That's the whole thing. It isn't even a story. It's about four seconds and I've built my entire life around four seconds.

choices.choice_text: [Stay where you are. Let her set every step.]
[Hold out your hands. Don't reach for her.]
"There's something in my footage. I need to tell you here."

ep2_pool_full_trust.speaker: Fiz
ep2_pool_full_trust.text: (I don't move. Not toward her, not away. I stand in four feet of water and I let her do all of it.)

ep2_pool_full_trust.speaker: Riley Jones
ep2_pool_full_trust.text: You're really not going to help.

ep2_pool_full_trust.speaker: Riley Jones
ep2_pool_full_trust.text: ...Oh. That IS the help. That's — okay. Okay, that's actually clever, don't look pleased with yourself.

ep2_pool_full_trust.speaker: Fiz
ep2_pool_full_trust.text: (Second step. Third. She comes out to where it's chest-deep entirely on her own and I have not moved a single centimetre in four minutes.)

ep2_pool_contact.speaker: Fiz
ep2_pool_contact.text: (I put my hands out, palms up, and leave them there. I don't close the distance. She has to be the one who closes the distance.)

ep2_pool_contact.speaker: Fiz
ep2_pool_contact.text: (Her fingers go around my wrists instead of my hands. Tighter than she needs to. She walks herself out to chest depth holding on to a thing that isn't moving.)

ep2_pool_confession.speaker: Riley Jones
ep2_pool_confession.text: ...Now? You're doing this now? I'm standing in a swimming pool having the worst hour of my month.

ep2_pool_confession.speaker: Fiz
ep2_pool_confession.text: (Ninety seconds, on a phone, at the edge of a pool at midnight. Her face lit up from underneath by eleven frames of fog going the wrong way.)

ep2_pool_confession.speaker: Riley Jones
ep2_pool_confession.text: I want to do the thing I came here to do, and then I want to be very frightened about the other thing. In that order. I've decided.

ep2_pool_confession.speaker: Fiz
ep2_pool_confession.text: (She reorganised the whole night in about nine seconds. I don't think she knows she can do that.)

ep2_pool_unspoken.speaker: Fiz
ep2_pool_unspoken.text: (Her name comes out and then nothing comes out after it.)

ep2_pool_unspoken.speaker: Fiz
ep2_pool_unspoken.text: (There's a version of this where I finish the sentence. I can see it. It's about four words long and I've had it loaded since roughly March.)

ep2_pool_unspoken.speaker: Riley Jones
ep2_pool_unspoken.text: You can just — keep that. For now. That's allowed.

ep2_pool_unspoken.speaker: Fiz
ep2_pool_unspoken.text: (She let me not say it. Of all the things she's done for me, that one goes near the top.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Right. I'm going to put my face in. Just my face. That's the entire ambition.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Don't count. If you count I'll kill you.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: TWO SECONDS. That was two seconds! That was — oh my God. Oh my GOD.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: I hate it. I hate it so much. I'm doing it again.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She's furious. She's laughing. Her hair's in her face and she's swearing at four feet of chlorinated water like it insulted her family.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (This is the best I have felt in a year and I am not going to be able to explain that to anyone, ever, including her.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (A flashlight crosses the far wall. Once, left to right, unhurried.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (It doesn't come back. Marcus does his rounds in eleven minutes and he has never once done them in twelve.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Was that —

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I shake my head. It's the first lie I've told her and it's a small one and she takes it.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Every surface in this house is a surface you could photograph. Nothing in it looks like anyone has ever put something down in a hurry.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Fiz! Riley's told me — well, Riley's mentioned you. Which from Riley is practically a speech.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Have you eaten? There's — I can do something. I can absolutely do something.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: He's fine, Elise.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Something goes across Elise's face and then gets tidied away, the same way everything in here gets tidied away.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Of course. Well. I'll be in the — yes.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Theo is on the stairs. He's been on the stairs the whole time. I don't know how long the whole time is.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Theodore Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Hey.

choices.choice_text: [Go and sit on the stairs with Theo.]
[Find Elise in the kitchen. Say yes to the food.]
[Look at the door at the end of the hall.]

ep2_theo_opens_slightly.speaker: Fiz
ep2_theo_opens_slightly.text: (I sit two steps below him and don't say anything. It takes about a minute and a half.)

ep2_theo_opens_slightly.speaker: Theodore Jones
ep2_theo_opens_slightly.text: Everyone asks me stuff. 'How's school.' 'How are you doing.' They've got a face they do first.

ep2_theo_opens_slightly.speaker: Theodore Jones
ep2_theo_opens_slightly.text: This house is really quiet at night. Like, wrong quiet. Dad works late in the office and he doesn't put the hall light on when he comes up.

ep2_theo_opens_slightly.speaker: Theodore Jones
ep2_theo_opens_slightly.text: That's not a thing. I just noticed it.

ep2_theo_opens_slightly.speaker: Fiz
ep2_theo_opens_slightly.text: (Nine words would have been generous. He gave me about sixty and then looked frightened of having done it.)

ep2_elise_softens.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
ep2_elise_softens.text: Oh — really? Right. Right, okay, good, I'll do the thing with the — you'll like it, it's nothing.

ep2_elise_softens.speaker: Fiz
ep2_elise_softens.text: (She cooks like someone who has been waiting a long time for a reason to.)

ep2_elise_softens.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
ep2_elise_softens.text: She doesn't hate me, you know. I know it looks like that. She just — she was fifteen and I was a project meeting.

ep2_elise_softens.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
ep2_elise_softens.text: Sorry. God. You're seventeen, you didn't come here for this.

ep2_elise_softens.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
ep2_elise_softens.text: It's just very quiet in this house and you're the first person in about two years who said yes to anything.

ep2_elise_softens.speaker: Fiz
ep2_elise_softens.text: (I ate all of it. It was genuinely good. I told her so and she had to go and look at the sink for a second.)

ep2_office_noticed.speaker: Fiz
ep2_office_noticed.text: (End of the hall. Dark wood. Shut. Every other door in this house is open, including the bathroom.)

ep2_office_noticed.speaker: Fiz
ep2_office_noticed.text: (There's a keypad. Not a lock — a keypad, in a family home, on an interior door.)

ep2_office_noticed.speaker: Riley Jones
ep2_office_noticed.text: Not because — just don't. He counts the attempts. It emails him.

ep2_office_noticed.speaker: Fiz
ep2_office_noticed.text: (She knows the system well enough to warn me about it. She's known that for a while.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: So that's the house. That's it. That's the whole tour.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Everyone thinks it's going to be worse than it is. It's not worse. It's just — nothing ever happens in it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (A car we didn't hear arrive. The front door, and then a voice in the hall that makes Riley stop on the top step with one shoe half on.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Richard Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Gerald. I wasn't expecting — it's Sunday.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: It is. Beautiful house, Richard. You've done a great deal with it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Riley's hand closes around my sleeve. Neither of us decided to sit down and both of us are sitting down.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: The survey work on the east side of the bay. You signed off on the extension.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Richard Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: It's a routine geotechnical — it's soil composition, Gerald. It's for the foundations.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Of course. And how deep does soil composition go, these days?

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Richard Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: ...Fourteen metres.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Mm.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: You'll want to bring that up to six. Six is standard for foundations. Anything under six is prudence, anything over six is curiosity, and curiosity is expensive in a town this size.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He hasn't raised his voice once. He sounds like a man reading out a weather report to someone who asked.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Richard Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Gerald, that was ten years ago. Nobody is looking at—

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Richard.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Some things stay buried because the ground is heavy. Some things stay buried because people agree not to dig.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Only one of those is reliable, and you and I are both standing on it. Six metres.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Give my regards to Elise. And to your daughter — she's at Blackwell now, isn't she. Second year.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (That's the only sentence he says with any warmth in it, and it's the one with Riley in it.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Richard Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: ...Six metres. Yes.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (The door. The car. Then Riley's father standing alone in his own hallway for a long time, not moving.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I look at Riley. And Riley is not surprised. Frightened, yes. Sick, yes.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Not surprised.)

choices.choice_text: [Get the phone out. Record what's left of it.]
[Get Riley out of this house. Now.]

ep2_end_recorded.speaker: Fiz
ep2_end_recorded.text: (Nineteen seconds. Most of it is the door and a car starting. Eleven of those seconds have Gerald Cross's voice on them, clean.)

ep2_end_recorded.speaker: Fiz
ep2_end_recorded.text: (One-party consent isn't a thing in Oregon. I know that because I looked it up in October for a completely different reason, and I press record anyway.)

ep2_end_recorded.speaker: Riley Jones
ep2_end_recorded.text: You just made that a crime. You know that's a crime here.

ep2_end_protect.speaker: Fiz
ep2_end_protect.text: (Down the back stairs, through the utility room, out past the bins. She doesn't ask where we're going.)

ep2_end_protect.speaker: Riley Jones
ep2_end_protect.text: I'm fine. I'm fine, I'm — don't look at me like that, I'm fine.

ep2_end_protect.speaker: Riley Jones
ep2_end_protect.text: Okay, I'm not. Can we walk? Can we just walk for a bit and you do the thing where you don't say anything?

ep2_end_protect.speaker: Fiz
ep2_end_protect.text: (We walked for an hour and ten minutes. I didn't say anything. It's the only thing I'm reliably good at and tonight it was enough.)

ep2_end_riley_confronted.speaker: Riley Jones
ep2_end_riley_confronted.text: Not that. Not him. But that — that shape of conversation. I've heard it through this floor since I was about eleven.

ep2_end_riley_confronted.speaker: Riley Jones
ep2_end_riley_confronted.text: I know what my father is. I've known for years and I've never said it out loud to a single person, and now I've said it to you on a landing.

ep2_end_riley_confronted.speaker: Riley Jones
ep2_end_riley_confronted.text: So don't ask me again tonight. Ask me tomorrow and I'll tell you everything. Just not tonight.

ep2_end_riley_confronted.speaker: Fiz
ep2_end_riley_confronted.text: (She kept her word. That's the part I'd like on the record later, when it matters what kind of person she was.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Six metres. Fourteen metres. Eight metres of difference between a foundation survey and whatever is under the east side of that bay.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (A week ago I had eleven frames of fog. Tonight I have a number.)
